title: Rajma Masala

ingredients.title: For the Rajma
items: Red kidney beans (rajma) – 1½ cups (about 300 g), dried
Water – as needed for soaking and boiling

ingredients.title: For the Masala Base
items: Ghee – 2 tbsp (or vegetable oil for vegan preparation)
Tomatoes – 3 medium (about 250 g), finely chopped or pureed
Red chili powder – 1–1½ tsp, adjust to taste

ingredients.title: For Garnish
items: Fresh coriander leaves – a handful, chopped

instruction.title: Soak & Cook the Rajma
steps: Wash the rajma thoroughly and soak in plenty of water for 8–10 hours or overnight.
Drain and rinse the soaked beans.
Add fresh water, 1 tsp salt, bay leaf, cinnamon stick, and green cardamom.
Pressure cook until the rajma is soft but still intact: about 5–6 whistles on medium heat, or use an Instant Pot on high pressure for 35–40 minutes.
Drain the cooked rajma and reserve the cooking liquid.

instruction.title: Build the Masala
steps: Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat.
Add chopped onions and sauté until deeply golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and cook for 1–2 minutes until the raw aroma disappears.
Add slit green chilies and tomatoes.
Cook until the tomatoes break down completely and the ghee begins to separate from the masala.
Add coriander powder, cumin powder, red chili powder, and turmeric.
Sauté for 30–45 seconds to bloom the spices.

instruction.title: Simmer with Rajma
steps: Add the cooked rajma to the masala.
Pour in about 1½ cups of the reserved rajma cooking liquid.
Lightly mash a few rajma beans against the side of the pan to naturally thicken the gravy.
Simmer uncovered on low heat for 20–25 minutes, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking.
Add garam masala and crushed kasuri methi during the final few minutes.

instruction.title: Finish & Serve
steps: Adjust salt and consistency; the finished gravy should be thick and coating rather than watery.
Swirl in fresh cream if using for extra richness.
Garnish with freshly chopped coriander leaves.
Serve hot with steamed basmati rice, jeera rice, naan, or paratha.

chefTips: Soaking: Overnight soaking helps the rajma cook evenly and gives a creamier final texture.
Onions: Cook the onions until deeply golden for maximum depth and sweetness in the masala.
Gravy: Mashing a few beans into the sauce naturally thickens the rajma without adding flour or cream.
Consistency: Rajma gravy thickens as it rests, so keep it slightly looser if serving later.
Flavor: Kasuri methi added near the end provides a subtle restaurant-style aroma.
Serving: Rajma pairs especially well with steamed basmati rice, traditionally served as rajma chawal.
Smoky finish: For extra depth, use a dhungar technique with hot charcoal immediately before serving.
